λάχν-η , ἡ,
A.soft woolly hair, down, as of the first beard, “πρίν σφωϊν . . πυκάσαι γένυς εὐανθέϊ λάχνῃ”
Od. 11.320
; “ὅτε λάχναι νιν μέλαν γένειον ἔρεφον”
Pi. O. 1.68
; of the thin hair on Thersites' head, “ψεδνὴ δ᾽ ἐπενήνοθε λ.”
Il. 2.219
; of the soft nap or pile on cloth, “οὔλη δ᾽ ἐπενήνοθε λ.”
10.134
; of the scanty hairs on the elephant, Luc. Philops. 24 ; of the hair or fur of wild beasts, “λάχνῃ δέρμα κατάσκιον”
Hes. Op. 513
; of the bear's or polecat's fur, Opp. C. 3.140 , Nic. Th. 690 ; of sheep's wool, S. Tr. 690 , Opp. C. 2.379 ; of ox's hair, A.R. 1.325 : in pl., of the hedgehog's quills, Plu. 2.98d , Opp. H. 2.369 .
II. metaph., leafage, Nic. Al. 410 , Opp. H. 4.167 , 380 (pl.).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
